arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Malcolm Stewart argued the determination is not final agency action. He stated it does not order anyone to do or refrain from doing anything.
Stewart claimed the document does not alter anyone's legal rights and obligations. He emphasized the lack of binding force in the determination.
Justice Roberts questioned the finality of the Corps' determination. He noted the document describes nonspecial cases in specific sections.
Justice Alito asked about the reviewability of the determination under the EPA. He inquired about the distance between the issue and the core case.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Army Corps of Engineers issued a jurisdictional determination. This ruling identifies specific wetlands. Hawkes Company challenges the scope of this authority. The dispute centers on whether this document is final agency action.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on March 30, 2016.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Hawkes wants the Court to declare the Corps determination final. This would allow Hawkes to challenge the ruling in court.
The Corps wants the Court to declare the determination non-final. This would prevent immediate judicial review of the wetland ruling.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Hawkes argues the determination is final agency action. The company claims the document alters legal rights and obligations.
The Corps argues the determination is not final. The agency claims it does not order anyone to act or refrain from acting.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Alito asked if the determination is reviewable under the EPA. He questioned how far removed the issue is from the core case.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if the determination is final regarding the Corps. He questioned whether the document applies only to special case determinations.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal wetland regulation. It determines when private parties can challenge agency determinations. The outcome shapes the balance between federal authority and private property rights.
